models_evaluated: 36 open-weight general, open-weight medical, and frontier closed-source general LLMs (individual models not named in the text)

links.outcome: Gap between high benchmark accuracy and reasoning quality/stability in caregiving case studies
links.effect: Top-tier models exceeded 0.9 accuracy, yet case studies showed inconsistent reasoning quality and stability, indicating benchmark accuracy overstates domain competence.
links.quote: While top-tier models achieved high accuracies (>0.9), case studies revealed inconsistent reasoning quality and stability, highlighting a critical need for domain-specific improvement to enhance LLMs' knowledge and reasoning grounded in daily caregiving data.

unlisted_practices: Building domain-specific (ADRD) benchmarks from caregiving program content to evaluate LLM knowledge

screen.reason: The study develops and evaluates an automated LLM benchmark (ADRD-Bench) focused on Alzheimer's Disease and Related Dementias across 36 models, measuring accuracy and reasoning without testing a specific operational guardrail or deployment practice.
